subject: mathematics
question_text: If f: R→R satisfies f(x + y) = f(x) + f(y) for all x, y ∈ R and f(1) = 7, find Σ f(r), r = 1 to n.

mark_split.label: Build f(r) = 7r for every natural number r

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.15, chapter 2 FUNCTIONS, Very Short Answer question 24. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+1 shape gives one mark to building f(r) = 7r out of the given property, which is the whole idea of the question, and one to summing it, because a student who reaches f(r) = 7r and then misquotes the sum of the first n natural numbers has still done half the work. The property is used only for natural r, and the card says so in its written lines. Paper position: Maths-1A Section A runs Q1–Q10 at 2 marks each, all compulsory. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this — how you get f(r) from the given property, and how you finish the sum.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Build f(r) from the property
steps.margin_note: One mark for reaching f(r) = 7r. Show at least f(2) and f(3) before claiming the general form; a bare f(r) = 7r earns nothing.
steps.memory_tip: f(x + y) = f(x) + f(y) turns addition inside f into addition outside, so f of a whole number is that many copies of f(1).
lines: f(x + y) = f(x) + f(y) and f(1) = 7
Adding f(1) one more time each step,
f(r) = r f(1) for every r ∈ N.
f(1) = 7 ⇒ f(r) = 7r for every r ∈ N.

recall.must_convey: That putting x = y = 1 gives f(2) = 2f(1), repeating gives f(r) = r f(1), and f(1) = 7 makes f(r) = 7r for natural r.

since f of one is seven f of r is seven r

steps.why: The property is the only information given about f, so f(r) has to be built out of it. Writing r as 1 + 1 + … + 1 and applying the property r − 1 times is what produces f(r) = r f(1).
common_mistakes: Assuming f(x) = 7x for every real x from the start, instead of building f(r) for natural r from the property.
Writing f(2) = f(1)² or f(2) = f(1) + 1 instead of f(1) + f(1).
Stopping at f(r) = r f(1) and never putting f(1) = 7.

steps.label: Add the n terms
steps.margin_note: The second mark is the sum. Take the 7 outside and quote Σr = n(n + 1)/2; leave the answer as a single fraction.
steps.memory_tip: Every term carries the same factor 7, so pull it out and only the sum 1 + 2 + … + n is left, which is n(n + 1)/2.

recall.must_convey: That the sum is 7(1 + 2 + … + n), and using Σr = n(n + 1)/2 gives 7n(n + 1)/2.

steps.why: Once f(r) = 7r is known the question is an arithmetic sum, not a function question. The constant 7 comes out of the sum, and what is left is the standard sum of the first n natural numbers.
common_mistakes: Quoting Σr as n(n + 1) and dropping the 2 in the denominator.
Writing the answer as 7n, which adds one term instead of n terms.
Leaving the answer as 7(1 + 2 + … + n) without using the standard sum.
